headline.purpose: One per trail stop, with the carved extrusion.

title.purpose: Timeline entries, project board, wayside sign names.

sign.purpose: Signpost link labels; plates use the same face at 22-28px.

stencil.purpose: Things struck or carved: checkpoint stamps, year posts, badge names.

value.purpose: Game and stat numbers: HUD, cat stats, checkpoint counter.

label.purpose: Stat and HUD terms, plate distances, counter caption; speaker names and nameplates at 800.

lead.purpose: First paragraph of a stop, in paint.

shadows.name: board-lift
shadows.purpose: Trailhead board and cream project board standing off the ground.

shadows.name: plate-drop
shadows.purpose: Arrow plates; applied as filter because clip-path cuts box-shadow.

shadows.name: stamp-ring
shadows.purpose: Inner second ring of rubber stamps and collected badges.

shadows.name: stake-bevel
shadows.purpose: Shaded side of a wayside stake.

shadows.name: carved-extrusion
shadows.purpose: text-shadow on stop headlines only; never on boxes.

shadows.name: panel-drop
shadows.purpose: Game dialog; notice card uses 0 30px 60px -20px rgba(0,0,0,.8).

shadows.name: figure-drop
shadows.purpose: Animals and rider standing on the ground (filter).

shadows.name: floor-rim
shadows.purpose: Scene floor's timber edge and dark falloff.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Every object movement: plate and sign slides, button lift, bubble, stamp entrance.

motion.name: camera
motion.purpose: Scene camera moves and stops rising into place (rise: rotateX(-16deg) translateY(36px) to rest; motion only).

motion.name: sway
motion.purpose: Wayside signs settling after scroll wind (rotateY up to 22deg, bottom-hinged).

motion.name: stamp-flip
motion.purpose: Checkpoint stamp flips down (rotateY 180deg, scale 1.4) when a stop is reached.

motion.name: stamp-down
motion.purpose: Collected badges and counter marks strike in (scale 1.8, rotate -20deg).

motion.name: tilt
motion.purpose: Pointer tilt up to 10deg on wayside signs, project board, signpost signs, cat yard; fine pointers only.

motion.name: led
motion.purpose: Rack LED blink; alarm pulses at .5s.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All motion removed under prefers-reduced-motion; scripted tilt, sway, camera drift and stamp flip not attached.

narrative.overview:
The page is a trek through the Western Ghats, told in the material vocabulary of a forest department: enamel green boards with cream hand-painted capitals, mustard and rust arrow plates on a timber post, carved distance posts, rubber checkpoint stamps in rust ink, and a dashed mustard trail line running down warm, near-black loam. Every surface is a physical object you would pass on a path, and the reader moves down the trail line from board to checkpoint to signpost.

The trailhead is a clearing with a small server farm on it, built in CSS 3D: an isometric loam floor with a faint cream grid and a timber rim, racks as five-faced boxes with blinking LED columns, the enamel name board raised as a billboard on two timber legs, and flat-illustrated animals (each in a mustard hard hat) standing as camera-facing billboards with nameplates. Screen-space game UI sits over it in the same vocabulary: dark loam panels with a line border for the HUD, a cream double-framed dialog box for speech. Below it, the trail itself is gently three-dimensional: stops rise into place, signs sway in the wind of a fast scroll and lean toward the pointer, a cyclist rides the trail line with the scroll, and checkpoint stamps flip down as you reach them.

Density is low and the rhythm is long: each stop sits off the trail line with generous vertical travel between them. Type is tall condensed sign-painter capitals for everything that would be painted on a board, and a friendly humanist sans for everything that would be spoken. Objects are slightly hand-planted: signs tilt a degree or three, stamps are struck at an angle, stakes vary in height.

It rejects the hero-plus-cards developer homepage and the terminal costume of the previous version (archived at /v2/).
keyCharacteristics: Dark trail ground, signage carries all the colour.
Square-cornered painted boards with bolted corners; circles only for stamps and bolts.
Arrow-plate silhouettes for anything that leads somewhere.
Condensed uppercase display type on signs; Figtree for prose.
Soft, downward lift under signage; no rounded cards, no glass, no gradient fills (gradients only shade the bolt heads and light the 3D scene's loam).
Real CSS 3D for depth: the hero scene is a perspective world; on the trail, 3D is motion only and never hides content.

rules.name: The Paint On Signs Rule
rules.body: Saturated colour lives only on objects (boards, plates, stamps, posts, buttons, LEDs); the ground itself stays loam. Ground may be lit in loam tones (the scene's light pool) but never tinted with a hue.

rules.name: The Two Rusts Rule
rules.body: Rust is a fill under cream text; Rust Ink is a stroke or text colour on dark ground. Do not swap them: rust text on loam fails, rust-ink fill under cream fails.

rules.name: The One Of Each Rule
rules.body: In a set of plates or signs, green is the default; rust and mustard appear once each to break the run.

rules.name: The Painted Caps Rule
rules.body: Every display-face string is uppercase. Figtree is never uppercased.

rules.name: The Stencil Is For Stamps Rule
rules.body: The stencil face marks things that were struck or carved (stamps, year posts, badge names). It never sets headlines or prose.

rules.name: The Standing Sign Rule
rules.body: Shadows fall down, never sideways, and only under objects that stand on the trail. No sign hovers on a halo. The carved extrusion is the one stepped shadow, and it belongs to headline lettering, never to a box.

rules.name: The Motion-Only 3D Rule
rules.body: On the trail, 3D transforms (rise, sway, tilt, stamp flip) animate content that is already visible; nothing waits on an observer or a 3D state to be readable, and all of it is skipped under prefers-reduced-motion.

dos: Do make every new surface an object you could pass on a trail: an enamel board, a plate, a post, a stamp, a stake.
Do keep boards square-cornered and give them corner bolts and the board or sign lift.
Do use the arrow-plate silhouette for anything that navigates or links out, and slide it along its arrow on hover.
Do set every display-face string in uppercase Big Shoulders; set prose in Figtree at 18px/1.65 in stone, with the lead in paint.
Do use rust as a fill under cream and rust-ink as a stroke or text on ground.
Do keep focus visible as the 3px mustard outline at 4px offset, and honour prefers-reduced-motion.
Do put screen-space game UI on night panels (88% loam, 2px line border, square) and speech on the cream double-framed dialog.
Do keep 3D on the trail motion-only: content is readable before and without any transform.
donts: Don't use rounded rectangles or rounded cards; the only curves are full circles for stamps, badges and bolts.
Don't tint section backgrounds or put colour on the ground; colour belongs to signage.
Don't cast shadows sideways or add ambient glows to boards and signs; lift is downward only. The single glow in the system marks a golden fish in the cat game.
Don't reintroduce terminal styling, monospace costume, or the hero-plus-cards developer layout.
Don't use the stencil face for headlines or body text.
Don't use more than one rust and one mustard in a set of plates or signs.
